statement: A running model, not a calibrated one, and thinner than the wisteria model it began from. What the plant is made of (opposite leaves of a measured length, cymes on short side shoots from older stems, paired follicles that seldom set in Britain, the weeks it flowers) follows floras, the RHS and one three-year study of a ten-year-old plant on a pergola in Belgrade. How fast it grows, how thickly it clothes a lattice and how much of it flowers are assumptions chosen to agree with those descriptions; none has been measured on a plant in Britain. The numbers by which a shoot chooses its way over a structure are still the wisteria model's. Use its output to compare scenarios and to show what a design implies, not to predict dates, sizes or loads.

names.basis: One leaf form and one flower form, so none is named. The cymes stand out from the foliage on slender stalks 2 to 6 cm long (Flora of China), at the ends and in the upper leaf axils of short side shoots (Bean: 'usually on short lateral twigs'). The paired follicles hang: seen in photographs of fruiting plants (Wikimedia Commons, 'Fruit du faux jasmin'), not stated in a flora.

phenology.budburstDoy.basis: No dated British record of the start of growth was found. Placed in mid April (15 April) so that the year's first shoots are full grown by mid June, which is when a three-year study in Belgrade found shoots at 90% of their length with leaves fully open (Ocokoljic et al. 2026, Pak. J. Bot. 58(7), BBCH 39).

phenology.growthEndDoy.basis: Long twining shoots go on being made after flowering, through late summer; growth is taken to stop at the end of September. No dated source.

phenology.leafFlushDoy.basis: An evergreen: this only paces the opening of leaves on wood that was already there. New leaves from late April to mid June; the end is the Belgrade study's date for fully expanded leaves (Ocokoljic et al. 2026), which Britain may run later than.

phenology.autumnColourDoy.basis: Not acted on: the engine gives an evergreen leaf no change of colour. Recorded as the weeks in which the leaves take their winter bronze and red with the first cold (RHS: 'often turn deep bronze-red in winter'), mid November to mid December, for when it can be shown.

phenology.leafFallDoy.basis: Not acted on for an evergreen: a leaf stays for organs.leafLifespanYears. Kept at the end of the year only because every model carries the parameter.

phenology.floralInitiationDoy.basis: Flower buds are taken to show on the young side shoots from the start of June, a month before the first open. In photographs the cymes stand in green bud for weeks before any flower opens. No dated source.

phenology.flowerOpenDoy.basis: Cymes begin to open from the end of June to about 10 August, so that with the weeks each lasts the plant is in flower through July and August: Bean, 'produced in July and August'; RHS, 'mid to late summer'. In Belgrade the first tenth of the flowers were open on day 161 to 168 and the last petals fell on day 227 to 233 in two ordinary years (Ocokoljic et al. 2026); Britain is cooler, and the later British months are kept.

phenology.petalFallDoy.basis: Not acted on while phenology.flowerLastsDays is given: each cyme then goes over in its own time. Set to the span in which they do.

phenology.flowerLastsDays.basis: How long one cyme is in flower: its two to nine flowers (counted in Belgrade, Ocokoljic et al. 2026) open a few at a time. Chosen so that the whole plant flowers for about nine weeks, as it did there in two ordinary years (66 and 65 days from the first tenth open to the last petal fallen). Not timed on a single cyme.

extension.leaderMPerSeason.basis: RHS guide: 'relatively slow growing but can reach 4m (14ft) or more in favourable conditions'; Bean: 10 or 12 ft high on walls in the south and west, 'slow-growing when young'. The RHS record's band of 8 to 12 m in 5 to 10 years would need more than a metre a year and is not what British growers report; a retailer's 10 to 20 cm a year is slower than plants that fill a fence panel in five years. 0.7 m takes a main stem to the top of a 3 m support in its fifth or sixth season. Not measured.

extension.lateralMPerSeasonByOrder.basis: Side branches a little slower than the main stems, each order slower again. Scaled from the leader rate; not measured.

extension.whipMPerSeason.basis: The long twining shoots that an established plant throws out from its older stems in summer, which reach for something to wind round. They make their length within the season. Rate not measured.

extension.establishmentFactorByYear.basis: Slow to start: Bean, 'slow-growing when young'; RHS guide, established 'after two or three years'. Three seasons of reduced extension, the first at under a third. The factors themselves are not measured.

architecture.trunkStemStartYears.basis: A nursery plant comes as several stems tied to canes (RHS guide: 'trained onto bamboo canes'): two from the first season and a third from the base in the second. The number is a choice.

architecture.nurseryCaneM.basis: RHS guide: nursery plants are 'usually 60cm to 1.8m tall'. A plant from the lower half of that range.

architecture.maxBranchOrder.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

architecture.leaderLengthM.basis: A cap on the length of a main stem: from the RHS guide's '4m (14ft) or more' to the RHS record's 'about 9 m tall'. A height is not a route length, so this is a stand-in.

architecture.lateralLengthMByOrder.basis: Side branches run for metres: the RHS record gives a spread of 4 to 8 m. Scaled down by order; not measured.

architecture.lateralLengthSpread.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

architecture.lateralChanceByParentOrder.basis: It branches freely and 'will cover its support effectively on its own, twining and scrambling up and across' (RHS guide), so nearly every crossing of the lattice that a stem passes sends a branch along the other member. The chances are a choice.

architecture.budExtraDormancyChance.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

architecture.budExtraDormancyYears.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

architecture.maxStemsPerRoute.basis: Its slender stems wind round one another as well as round the support, so a lath or a cable carries a rope of several: seen in photographs of established plants (Wikimedia Commons, Starr 090416-5994 and 'Trachelospermum jasminoides A'). Four is a choice; not counted on plants.

architecture.maxStemsPerPrimaryMember.basis: One more than on a lath, as in the wisteria model, a glulam member being wide enough to lay more stems side by side.

routing.occupancyCost.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.downhillCostPerM.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.uphillBonusPerM.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.straightOnBonus.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.riserBonus.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.tierBonus.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.roleDropChance.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.noise.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.giveUpCost.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

attachment.maxGraspDiameterMm.basis: No measurement exists. Taken as well below the timber lattice (76 mm round) and above a cable, so that this plant twines cables unaided and has to be tied to glulam. The whole difference between it and wisteria on the structure rests on this number. What is recorded: it is sold wound on bamboo canes and the RHS asks for 'wires or trellis'.

attachment.minPitchM.basis: The rise of one turn round a thin support. Read off a photograph of stems on a bamboo cane (Wikimedia Commons, 'Trachelospermum jasminoides A'), where a turn takes several widths of the cane: a slack spiral, tighter than the wisteria model's 0.3 m because the stems are far more slender. Not measured.

attachment.pitchPerCircumference.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

organs.leafSpacingM.basis: No flora gives the length between leaf pairs. Read off photographs against the leaf lengths the floras give: half a leaf apart on the short flowering shoots, a leaf or more apart on long twining ones. One range has to serve both kinds of shoot.

organs.leafLengthM.basis: Ocokoljic et al. 2026, Pak. J. Bot. 58(7): 300 full-grown leaves of a ten-year-old plant on a pergola in Belgrade measured 4.20 to 8.80 cm long. The same species, cultivated outdoors in a climate with colder winters and hotter summers than Britain's; whether the stalk (3 to 12 mm, Flora of China) was included is not said. Flora of China gives the blade as 2 to 10 cm, Bean as 1 1/2 to 3 1/2 in.

organs.leavesPerNode.basis: NC State Extension plant record: leaf arrangement 'opposite'. The Belgrade study says the same of the leaves it measured.

organs.spurChance.basis: It makes no spurs. The short leafy shoots that clothe its older stems and carry its flowers are grown as flowering side shoots (sideShoots.*), which bear their leaves in pairs along their length; a spur in this engine is wisteria's, a tuft at one node that hangs clear of the timber.

organs.spurLengthM.basis: Not acted on while organs.spurChance is 0; present because every model carries every parameter.

organs.spurLeafCount.basis: Not acted on while organs.spurChance is 0; present because every model carries every parameter.

organs.racemeLengthM.basis: The length of a cyme from where its stalk leaves the shoot to its farthest flower. Flora of China: stalk 2 to 6 cm, to which the forks and the flowers add 2 to 3 cm; the Chinese flora (FRPS) says the cyme is as long as the leaf or longer. Bean's '1 1/2 to 2 in. long' is the short end. A range read from three descriptions that do not measure the same thing.

organs.whipShareOfNodes.basis: The share of older leaf nodes that throw a long twining shoot in a year. Photographs of established plants in summer show such shoots standing out of the foliage every few hand-widths; the share is a choice.

organs.whipsPerYearMax.basis: A cap on new long shoots a year, so that a large plant does not bristle. A choice.

organs.whipLengthM.basis: How far a long shoot reaches when it finds nothing to wind round, before it arches over and stops. Judged from photographs, where free shoots stand a few leaf lengths to an arm's length out of the plant. Not measured; see the species profile on how such shoots really behave.

organs.leafLifespanYears.basis: Evergreen and leathery, but no source read says how long a leaf lives. Three seasons assumed; older leaves are seen yellowing and reddening before they fall, and cold may strip them sooner (RHS guide: in cold snaps leaves 'may turn red, develop spots, or fall').

organs.clearStemHeightM.basis: Clothed nearly to the ground while young; side shoots are not thrown from the lowest hand-width of stem. A choice.

flowering.competenceYears.basis: Nursery plants are sold in flower, so it flowers young. In the model its first flowering side shoots break from the cane it arrived with in its second season.

flowering.maturityRamp.basis: Flowering builds up while the plant establishes (RHS guide: established 'after two or three years'). The steps are a choice.

flowering.spurFloralChance.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.unprunedFactor.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.currentSeasonFlowersPerM.basis: Cymes in the leaf axils of the year's long growth. Flora of China has the cymes 'terminal and axillary'; Bean has them 'usually on short lateral twigs', so the long shoots carry few. Two to the metre is a choice; most of the flowers are on the side shoots.

flowering.currentSeasonMinShootM.basis: A shoot shorter than this is taken not to flower in its leaf axils. A placeholder.

pruning.summerLeavesKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

pruning.winterBudsKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

regrowth.shootsPerCut.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

thickening.tipRadiusSquaredMm2.basis: A young shoot about 2.5 mm thick: read off photographs against leaves of known length. No flora gives the thickness of a shoot.

thickening.radiusSquaredPerMetreMm2.basis: Stems stay slender: chosen so that the main stems of a ten-year-old plant on the specimen frame are about as thick as a thumb at the base. No measured stem diameters were found.

thickening.branchShare.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

fruit.setShare.basis: RHS guide: 'fruits and seeds are rarely produced in UK gardens'; in Belgrade none set in three years (Ocokoljic et al. 2026). One cyme in fifty is this model's reading of 'rarely': a handful of pods on an established plant in a year, many plants having none.

fruit.lengthM.basis: Flora of China 16: 167 (efloras.org taxon 200018474, read from the copy at this address because efloras.org refused the request): 'Follicles linear, 10-25 cm x 3-10 mm'. One fruit here is the pair of follicles that follows one flower.

fruit.swellDays.basis: Days for the follicles to reach their length after the flower goes over. No source times it; chosen so that pods from August flowers are full length by late autumn.

fruit.ripenDoy.basis: Flora of China gives fruit from June to December in China, where it flowers from March. In Britain it flowers three months later; the green pods are taken to turn brown in December. No British record of ripening was found.

fruit.fallDoy.basis: The dry follicles split along one side and let their plumed seeds go; taken to happen from mid January to mid March, so that pods hang through the winter. Not recorded for Britain.

appendages.tendrilNodePattern.basis: It has no tendrils: a twiner that holds on with its stems (RHS: 'with twining stems'). No description read mentions any.

appendages.leafStalkCoilShare.basis: Its leaf stalks are 3 to 12 mm long (Flora of China) and do not clasp: it holds on with its stems.

appendages.prickleSpacingM.basis: Unarmed: no description read mentions prickles or thorns.

sideShoots.bearingWoodAgeYears.basis: The flowering shoots break from wood made in earlier years: Huxley and Davis, as reported by Useful Temperate Plants, 'flowers are produced on short laterals that arise from old wood'; Bean, 'usually on short lateral twigs'. Last year's stems are old enough.

sideShoots.perMetrePerYear.basis: How thickly the older stems are set with short flowering shoots. Chosen so that an established stem carries one at most of its leaf nodes, as photographs of plants in flower show, and a lattice it has covered reads as a screen (RHS lists it for 'hedging and screens'). Not counted on plants.

sideShoots.lengthM.basis: 'Short lateral twigs' (Bean): one to four pairs of leaves below the cyme in photographs, which at the leaf spacing above is a hand-width or so. Not measured.

sideShoots.lifespanYears.basis: The short shoots are woody and stay: on the plant they branch again and flower from their own side shoots in later years, which this model shows as the same shoot flowering again. Four seasons is a choice, a little longer than a leaf is taken to last.

sideShoots.terminalFlowerShare.basis: Most short shoots of an established plant in sun end in a cyme: in photographs of plants in full flower few are without one. The share is a choice, and takes no account of shade, which the profiles say reduces flowering.
